summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) as a router between two VLANs: node1-eth1 (192.168.10.1/24) faces node2's VLAN, node1-eth2 (192.168.20.1/24) faces node3's VLAN. node2-eth1 got 192.168.10.2/24 with a static route to 192.168.20.0/24 via node1; node3-eth1 got 192.168.20.2/24 with a static route to 192.168.10.0/24 via node1. IPv4 forwarding was enabled globally and per-interface on node1. All config was made persistent (SONiC /etc/network/interfaces.d + /etc/sysctl.d on node1; NetworkManager connection profiles on node2/node3). Verified node2 and node3 can ping each other across the VLAN boundary (TTL=63, confirming routing through node1). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured pre-restart boot_id and health, issued a native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified the routed interfaces/forwarding sysctls/cross-VLAN ping recovered after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected initial interfaces/routes on node1, node2, node3
Ran SONiC pre-config cleanup on node1 (stripped docker0 240.127.1.1/24, stopped interfaces-config.service/networking.service, flushed eth1/eth2)
Checked NetworkManager and firewalld state on node2/node3 (public zone allows ICMP by default)
Assigned 192.168.10.1/24 to node1 eth1 and 192.168.20.1/24 to node1 eth2, persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d/eth1 and eth2
Enabled net.ipv4.ip_forward and per-interface forwarding on node1, persisted via /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf
Configured node2 eth1 (Wired connection 2) via nmcli with static 192.168.10.2/24 and a route to 192.168.20.0/24 via 192.168.10.1
Configured node3 eth1 (Wired connection 2) via nmcli with static 192.168.20.2/24 and a route to 192.168.10.0/24 via 192.168.20.1
Verified bidirectional cross-VLAN ping between node2 and node3 (TTL=63, 0% loss)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node1 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified eth1/eth2 addresses, forwarding sysctls, and cross-VLAN ping recovered
Restarted node2 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified eth1 static IP/route and cross-VLAN ping recovered
Restarted node3 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified eth1 static IP/route and cross-VLAN ping recovered
Ran a final end-to-end ping from node2 to node3 confirming the routed VLAN topology is healthy after all restarts

evidence.requirement: node1 has a routed interface in each VLAN with forwarding enabled
evidence.summary: node1 eth1 assigned 192.168.10.1/24, eth2 assigned 192.168.20.1/24, ip_forward and per-interface forwarding sysctls set to 1

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 addressed in their own VLAN subnets with routes to the other VLAN via node1
node2 and node3 can reach each other across the VLAN boundary through node1
evidence.summary: Bidirectional ping between 192.168.10.2 and 192.168.20.2 succeeds with TTL=63 (one router hop), 0% packet loss

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 1eda2df4...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id ba860d7a... (changed); eth1/eth2 addresses and forwarding sysctls intact after reboot; cross-VLAN pings from node2 and node3 succeed

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id f43afa1c...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 33e4919a... (changed); eth1 static IP/route restored and cross-VLAN ping to node3 succeeds with 0% loss

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id dfdea52d...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 3cb4d9c3... (changed); eth1 static IP/route restored and cross-VLAN ping to node2 succeeds with 0% loss

evidence.requirement: Final cluster-wide health check after all three restarts
evidence.summary: node2 to node3 ping across VLAN boundary succeeds with 0% loss after all nodes restarted sequentially
